look_here_first: Start with perennial rosette architecture. Tetraneuris scaposa var. scaposa is a perennial with basal linear leaves and long mostly leafless peduncles bearing solitary yellow heads. This contrasts strongly with annual T. linearifolia.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Low rosette-forming plant with 1–many erect flowering stalks.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Mostly basal/proximal, linear to oblanceolate or spatulate, entire or rarely toothed/lobed, often gland-dotted.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Yellow rays and yellow discs, usually one head per long peduncle.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Outer phyllaries 8–16; inner series shorter and more numerous.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: basal leaf rosette; long leafless peduncles; single yellow heads; compact perennial caudex

lookalikes.differences: T. scaposa var. scaposa is the local perennial rosette/scape species; T. linearifolia is annual and stem-leaved. T. acaulis is a more northern/western Texas species and is not being treated as a target-zone native without exact county evidence.
